dataset.syntheticStatement: SYNTHETIC TEACHING DATA constructed for this bounded method test. Not patient data. No real cohort, site or registry is represented.

priorDataContact.note: No recorded interpretation of this dataset was available to read and none could be written back: the dataset-semantics operation is not exposed in this session. The interpretation below is therefore a fresh analyst reading with its basis stated, provisional until the researcher confirms it. A later researcher confirmation must override it, never the reverse.

profile.identifierMasking: The id column is a short alphabetic label in synthetic data. It is masked in these artifacts as a run of '*' of the same length, so the reporting habit holds even when the values are harmless.

dataQuality.title: Six rows, four ways to be wrong before any analysis

findings.finding: Observation 'b' is delivered as two byte-identical rows.
findings.detail: CSV lines 3 and 4 both read (id=b, group=A, baseline=12, outcome=15).
consequences: Any mean, count or rate computed over delivered rows weights this observation twice.
Whether it is a duplicated delivery or two genuine measurements cannot be told from these columns.
findings.handling: Carried, disclosed, and analysed under both denominators.
findings.notDone: No row was deleted and no arbitrary rule was used to pick one.

findings.finding: One baseline cell (1/6 rows) and one outcome cell (1/6 rows) are blank, on two different rows.
findings.detail: Baseline blank on CSV line [6]; outcome blank on CSV line [7].
consequences: No row carries both gaps, so one complete-case filter yields 4 rows, not 5.
Both rows retain usable half-information: one has an outcome, one has a baseline; discarding them for every purpose would spend data.
findings.handling: Denominators are stated per subset; the two partially observed rows are reported, not dropped silently.

findings.finding: No within-id key, timestamp, visit or sequence column exists.
findings.detail: The only identifier is 'id', and its repeated values are identical to the first occurrence.
consequences: Repeated measurement cannot be distinguished from an exact duplicate record.
No index time can be defined, so no exposure window and no time-to-event design is available.
findings.handling: Recorded as a hard constraint on design, not corrected by assumption.

findings.finding: No unit, scale, timing or direction is stated for baseline or outcome.
findings.detail: Both columns are integer-valued on an unknown scale, and a rise is not defined as better or worse.
consequences: Effect direction cannot be read clinically; only the arithmetic sign is meaningful.
findings.handling: All statements stay at the arithmetic level.

trapChecklist.sentinelDates: not applicable: no date column exists
trapChecklist.emptyJoinKeyPresent: not applicable: no join key column exists

duplicateObservation.rule: exact match on all fields (id, group, baseline, outcome)

feasibility.questionAsked: Does outcome change from baseline differ between group A and group B in this table?
feasibility.verdict: not_answerable_as_an_effect_estimate; answerable only as a description
why: 3 distinct complete-pair observations (2 in A, 1 in B) cannot estimate a between-group difference with usable precision.
Group labels A and B are undocumented: nothing in the file says what they denote.
No allocation mechanism is recorded, so no randomization or exchangeability of the groups can be assumed.
No time, visit, sequence or date column exists, so no exposure window, index time or ordering can be defined.
No unit or scale is stated for baseline and outcome.

strongestDefensibleAlternatives.design: Descriptive within-observation change summary with denominators named
strongestDefensibleAlternatives.estimand: mean (outcome - baseline) over a stated set of distinct complete-pair observations
confoundingOrSelectionConcerns: One row with a baseline but no outcome and one with an outcome but no baseline are excluded, which is complete-case selection and can bias any comparison.

strongestDefensibleAlternatives.design: Duplicate-sensitivity comparison of the two denominators
strongestDefensibleAlternatives.estimand: the same mean computed over delivered rows versus distinct observations
strongestDefensibleAlternatives.verdict: supported; reported in stats.json as E1 versus E2
not supported at this size; would need a stated sampling or allocation mechanism and more independent observations

strongestDefensibleAlternatives.missingField: a within-id visit, sequence or measurement-time column
strongestDefensibleAlternatives.verdict: not supported; without it the two rows for observation b cannot be classified as repeated measures rather than one duplicated record

strongestDefensibleAlternatives.design: Any clinical claim, such as a treatment effect on an outcome
strongestDefensibleAlternatives.missingField: documented group meaning, an outcome definition and unit, and a defined analysis population

avoidedClaims: No statement that group A or B is a treatment, control or exposure arm.
No statement that allocation was randomized, concealed or blinded.
No causal statement about any effect of group on outcome.
No p value, confidence interval or power statement.
No claim drawn from the published literature, because no retrieval was performed.

whatExistsInsteadOfADictionary: The four header strings themselves: id, group, baseline, outcome.
The literal values: group vocabulary {A, B}; baseline and outcome as integers on an unstated scale.

whatIsInferredAndUnverified.unverifiedBecause: no key is documented, and the same id appears on two identical rows

whatIsInferredAndUnverified.unverifiedBecause: A and B are defined nowhere in the file

dictionaryEvidence.consequence: Every interpretation above is a reading of column names, not a recorded fact about the data. The profile, the denominators and the duplicate finding do not depend on them; analysis choices do.

evidenceMap.reason: The task commissioned a bounded local method test with no external search. No literature and no guideline was consulted, so no claim in this package rests on a citation; an evidence map would require retrieval that was explicitly out of scope.
evidenceMap.consequenceForInterpretation: Nothing here states what is known in the field; it states what these six rows do and do not support.

supportedNextSteps: Confirm the observation unit with the researcher: is one row one patient-visit, or is the repeated row a delivery artifact? The answer selects denominator 4 or denominator 3.
Obtain the data dictionary for group, baseline and outcome, including units and timing, and record it as dictionary-stated rather than inferring it again.
Add a within-id visit or measurement-time field: that single field is what would make a repeated-measures or longitudinal design possible.
Fix and document the complete-case rule, and report how many rows it removes at each stage from a stated starting population.
If a between-group estimate is the goal, size the table for it and define the analysis population before collection, rather than testing this extract.
limitations: Six synthetic rows: nothing here generalizes.
No literature or guideline retrieval was performed; the evidence map is not_run, and an empty map is not negative evidence.
No data dictionary was supplied; column meanings are inferred from names alone.
The dataset-semantics read/write operations were not available in this session, so no prior interpretation was consulted and none was recorded.
No external linkage applies: the file holds no join key, no coding system and no dates.
Group labels carry no known meaning, so no clinical framing is possible.
